messages.author: dcf9816d9381783f
messages.subject: auxiliary variables in Nimble code
parts:
Hi all,

I'm translating the Stan code from this publication into Nimble, and I have a question regarding Nimble coding practices. There's a block of Stan code that uses an extra int type variable "count" to simplify subsetting of a multidimensional object into a linear array, here:

generated quantities {
  real p_avg;
  vector[J] p_pop; // population prevalence in the J poststratification cells
  int count;
  count = 1;
  for (i_zip in 1:N_zip) {
    for (i_age in 1:4) {
      for (i_eth in 1:4) {
        for (i_male in 0:1) {
          p_pop[count] = inv_logit(b[1]
          + b[2] * i_male
          + b[3] * x_zip[i_zip]
          + a_eth[i_eth]
          + a_age[i_age]
          + a_zip[i_zip]);
          count += 1;
        }
      }
    }
  }
  p_avg = sum(N_pop .* p_pop) / sum(N_pop);
}

In Nimble, I've used the classic C multidimensional indexing technique to convert the loop indices into the linear array, but it's long, confusing, and prone to error when more variables are added, is there a better way to do this?

# post-stratified prevalence 
for (i_zip in 1:N_zip) {
  for (i_age in 1:4) {
    for (i_eth in 1:4) {
      for (i_male in 0:1) {
        p_pop[(((i_zip-1) * 4*4*2) + ((i_age-1) * 4*2) + ((i_eth-1) * 2) + i_male) + 1] <- ilogit(b[1]         + b[2] * i_male + b[3] * x_zip[i_zip] + a_eth[i_eth] + a_age[i_age] + a_zip[i_zip])
      }
    }
  }
}
p_avg <- inprod(N_pop[],p_pop[]) / sum(N_pop[])

Thanks for the help!

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: auxiliary variables in Nimble code
parts:
hi Sean,

The model code in nimble is declarative rather than imperative, so the Stan-style incrementing won't work.

You could set up p_pop as a 4-d array so that you index each element separately and don't need to do the arithmetic. Though if you do that, then you wouldn't be able to use inprod() directly on a single vector (1-d array) as you are now. 

-chris

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: auxiliary variables in Nimble code
parts:
Hi Sean,

Thanks for the question and good to see this application.

Another option would be to use

p_pop[ count_index[ i_zip, i_age, i_eth, i_male ] ]  <- ilogit (...)

You can set up the indexing in count_index in R and provide it to nimbleModel in the constants list.  That might reduce the potential for confusion and preserve the setup that is otherwise useful to you.  Let me know if the idea is not clear.

-Perry
